turns.maya: I'm Maya. I'm 28 and live in Toronto. I've been tired lately, and I'd like to understand my periods better.
turns.stellis: Start with the Cycle tracker so your period dates and flow have a home.

turns.maya: I'd like to see my family doctor about the tiredness.
turns.stellis: Add your primary-care appointment to the calendar.
turns.title: Maya: primary-care appointment

turns.maya: I've seen my doctor and collected my 2022 reports. Can you help me keep them together?
turns.stellis: Upload the 2022 demo ZIP in the demo box.

turns.maya: These are visits and tests from different days. I want them in the right order.
turns.stellis: The dates of your visits and tests are filled from the reports.

turns.maya: My reports cover low iron and period health as well as routine care.
turns.stellis: Review the suggested notebooks before adding them to Maya’s empty library.

turns.maya: My hemoglobin was normal but my ferritin was low. I'd like to see the follow-up results together.
turns.stellis: Open the timeline and compare January and May with the August review.

turns.maya: My iron repletion follow-up says my ferritin improved. Can you explain what changed during 2022 using my reports?
turns.stellis: Ask Stellis with Preventive Care selected and inspect the source links.

turns.maya: I'm feeling better, and we're thinking about trying for a baby next year.
turns.stellis: Return to My Health to see the notebooks, cycle log and records you added.

turns.maya: We've been trying for a baby since January. I'm still tracking my periods.
turns.stellis: Add the June period to the same Cycle history.

turns.maya: My family doctor has referred me to a fertility clinic. I'd like help getting ready.
turns.stellis: Add the fertility intake appointment to your calendar.
turns.title: Maya: fertility intake

turns.maya: I've now had the intake, blood tests and an ultrasound. Here are my 2023 records.
turns.stellis: Upload the 2023 demo ZIP alongside the earlier demo history.

turns.maya: Can we separate the test dates from the dates I reviewed them with the clinic?
turns.stellis: Review the visit and test dates found in the reports.

turns.maya: I'd like a place for fertility care without losing my general health history.
turns.stellis: Add Fertility and reuse Menstrual Health where the reports overlap.

turns.maya: I want to take the hormone results and ultrasound findings to my next visit.
turns.stellis: Use the timeline’s document and notebook filters to review the investigations.

turns.maya: My mid-luteal progesterone was tested. What does my report document, and what investigations were still pending?
turns.stellis: Ask from the Fertility notebook and follow the citations.

turns.maya: We've decided to go ahead with IVF. The clinic confirmed my retrieval after the trigger instructions.
turns.stellis: Add the confirmed retrieval time to the calendar.
turns.title: Maya: egg retrieval

turns.maya: One treatment cycle is a lot to keep track of. I've collected the monitoring, retrieval and transfer records from 2024.
turns.stellis: Upload the 2024 demo ZIP to extend the existing history.

turns.maya: Some reports were written after the procedure. Please help me keep the clinical dates straight.
turns.stellis: Review the visit and procedure dates filled from your reports.

turns.maya: Can I keep IVF together while retaining the connection to my fertility investigations?
turns.stellis: Review the new IVF notebook and the existing Fertility notebook.

turns.maya: The retrieval and embryology reports describe different stages. I'd like to see them in sequence.
turns.stellis: Open the embryo culture report from the timeline.

turns.maya: My cryopreservation report is here. How many eggs were retrieved, mature and normally fertilized, and how many blastocysts were frozen?
turns.stellis: Ask Stellis from Fertility and check the four counts against the report.

turns.maya: The November transfer led to a positive pregnancy test and then an ultrasound. The clinic gave me a due date.
turns.stellis: Add the estimated due date as a milestone with its estimated status.
turns.title: Maya: estimated due date

turns.maya: My priorities are changing from fertility treatment to pregnancy care.
turns.stellis: Review how My Health has grown while keeping the earlier history available.

turns.maya: I'm pregnant and have an anatomy ultrasound booked. I'd like to keep the appointment with my other care.
turns.stellis: Add the March ultrasound appointment to the calendar.
turns.title: Maya: anatomy ultrasound

turns.maya: I've collected my prenatal, birth and postpartum reports from 2025. I'd like to make sense of this year.
turns.stellis: Upload the 2025 demo ZIP to bring these records into the same demo history.

turns.maya: There are screening dates, visits, the birth and later follow-ups.
turns.stellis: Confirm the dates filled from your reports.

turns.maya: Pregnancy and recovery now deserve their own places, but my iron history still matters.
turns.stellis: Review Pregnancy, Birth Preparation and Postpartum Recovery alongside the existing notebooks.

turns.maya: My anatomy scan was reassuring. I want to understand the difference between screening and a diagnosis.
turns.stellis: Review the scan and prenatal screening sources from the timeline.

turns.maya: My maternal discharge summary is here. Can you help me review the birth and my recovery using that report?
turns.stellis: Ask from Postpartum Recovery and inspect the discharge citation.

turns.maya: My baby was born on July 29. I'd like the calendar to distinguish the actual birth from the estimated due date.
turns.stellis: Confirm the birth date in the existing milestone instead of changing the estimate.

turns.maya: I'm recovering after birth and following up on iron and pelvic health. I haven't resumed periods yet.
turns.stellis: Review postpartum care in My Health while keeping lochia separate from period tracking.

years.title: Finding a new routine
years.summary: Periods return and routine care resumes

turns.maya: My first period after birth started on January 12. I'd like to resume tracking without counting postpartum bleeding as a period.
turns.stellis: Log the January period in Cycle with its actual start and end.
turns.note: First postpartum period; light to moderate flow

turns.maya: I've felt tired again and want to discuss my periods and iron with my family doctor.
turns.stellis: Add the June review to the calendar.
turns.title: Maya: fatigue and menstrual review

turns.maya: I've collected my screening, repeat iron tests and annual review from 2026.
turns.stellis: Upload the final yearly demo ZIP.

turns.maya: I'd like this year’s tests and treatment reviews to stay in clinical date order.
turns.stellis: Confirm the extracted dates from the reports.

turns.maya: These records belong with the health history I've already built.
turns.stellis: Review the existing notebooks and file the new items without making duplicates.

turns.maya: My ferritin fell again and improved with follow-up. I want to compare the results across years.
turns.stellis: Open the annual review and compare it with earlier iron results.

turns.maya: My annual review says my latest ferritin is 48. What is the documented iron plan and the last-dose date?
turns.stellis: Ask from Preventive Care and check the dated source.

turns.maya: I can now see five years of my health together, from routine care through fertility treatment and becoming a parent.
turns.stellis: Review the complete demo history or clear it in one action when you finish.
